chunks: 1340 - And I heard our shaykh, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may Allah be pleased with him, say: It was narrated that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked
about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you that you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may afflict you.”
So he عليه السلام said: “This is a second shortening, and it is that a man reduces two rakʿahs to one.”

key_terms.إِنْ خِفْتُمْ: if you are in a state of fear
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) being discussed in the verse
key_terms.تَقْصِيرٌ: shortening of the salat (prayer) in a legally prescribed form

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about shortening the prayer during fear mean according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic verse on shortening the salat (prayer) during fear while traveling as referring to a second kind of shortening. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that in this case, the worshipper reduces two rakʿahs to one, clarifying a specific legal form of salat al-khawf.
